items.title: Empowering Combatant Commands: The Role of Maven Smart System and Palantir Builder Bootcamps
items.hover_description:
Hands-On Building for Real-World Applications

Maven Smart System (MSS) is a proven CJADC2 system used by the Joint Staff, Combatant Commands, Armed Services, and various elements throughout the Department of War (DoW) and Intelligence Community. Powered by the Palantir Platform and backed by DoW’s Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO), MSS has proven to be a game-changer for the defense community as it helps connect, operationalize, and accelerate artificial intelligence adoption at all stages of the defense decision-making lifecycle.

The MSS platform ingests and integrates data from all sensors — satellites, drones, ground-based radar, HUMINT, etc. — providing users with a near-real-time, synchronized view of the battlespace. Its advanced software and AI capabilities synthesize, analyze, and translate vast amounts of data into legible, relevant, and actionable insights for analysts, warfighters, and decision-makers. Additionally, the platform supports rapid communication across all services and domains, enabling swift and decisive action.

“Through our collaboration with the Department of War on Maven Smart System, our hands-on training equips Combatant Commands with cutting-edge AI capabilities, empowering military units to tackle real-world challenges with enhanced precision and effectiveness.” — Akash Jain, President and CTO of Palantir USG

To equip the growing number of MSS users across the Combatant Commands, Palantir has been conducting Builder Bootcamps. The workshops are designed to empower users with the skills and tools necessary to fully optimize and build within the MSS platform, helping to advance specific mission needs and tackle real-world challenges.

Benefits of Builder Bootcamps

Builder Bootcamps have been effective in equipping operators and analysts with the skills and tools needed to utilize MSS to its fullest potential through hands-on training in advanced AI and data integration tools. By exploring both simplified and advanced workflows, participants across the technical spectrum gain practical experience and insights, allowing them to develop tailored solutions to improve operational efficiency and decision-making within their commands.

The Bootcamps range from one to four days, with curriculum tailored to participants’ abilities, roles, and mission-specific needs. Generally, sessions begin with briefings on the MSS platform and its capabilities before delving into hands-on builder training on specific tools, with time after the sessions for additional workshopping of mission-driven required solutions.
During these Bootcamps, core concepts and tools such as Pipeline Builder, Workshop, AIP Logic, Contour, and Code Workspaces are discussed. With a focus on hands-on building, attendees leverage their own ontology that synthesizes real-world data, logic, and action. Palantir engineers serve as trainers, helping participants launch their own versions of various established templates, focusing on core concepts and reinforcing how to install and leverage these for their own workflows. Typically, participants install the template in their bootcamp sandbox, tackle a simple task by modifying the template, and then receive one-on-one assistance in a Teaching Assistant style.

After the day’s sessions conclude, participants have the opportunity to work one-on-one with MSS engineers to tackle some of the harder problems they face in their day-to-day roles, and map out how Foundry tools could help address those challenges. For example, one user shared that they had been struggling for months to map radar coverage over custom areas of interest and report percent-coverage metrics. Using Pipeline Builder, an MSS trainer helped them create a solution in minutes.

These bootcamps have not only enhanced user proficiency but also generated interest in further MSS development and adoption.

Building Across Combatant Commands and Operational Units

Palantir is delivering intensive bootcamps directly to combatant commands and tactical units worldwide, equipping MSS users with the skills to independently build solutions for real-world operational challenges they face in theater. From CENTCOM’s counter-terrorism operations to AFRICOM’s stability missions, from INDOPACOM’s maritime security challenges to EUCOM’s deterrence efforts, and including specialized training with the Army’s XVIII Airborne Corps, these bootcamps are transforming users into builders.

Building with CENTCOM

Palantir’s collaboration with CENTCOM has highlighted the potential of hands-on training and advanced data integration tools. The inaugural bootcamp in 2024 began with a surprise appearance by CENTCOM’s Chief Data Officer, who joined in building for the majority of the six-hour session. This engagement set a positive tone and underscored the initiative’s importance.

Following the success of the first CENTCOM Builder Bootcamp, CENTCOM leadership requested that Palantir offer recurring bootcamps to reach as many builders in the command as possible — and Palantir is delivering.

The Palantir team recently hosted a two-day Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) bootcamp at CENTCOM, featuring tailored sessions for General Officers / Flag Officers as well as a comprehensive five-hour Builder Bootcamp designed for everyday MSS users, operators, and data engineers.

Across both days, Palantir engineers introduced 60 participants to the Palantir AI Platform on MSS, focusing on teaching them how to effectively integrate it into their daily workflows. The sessions covered a wide range of platform capabilities, culminating in collaborative brainstorming to identify potential applications within their respective roles and directorates. Toward the end, attendees teamed up with MSS engineers to bring their ideas to life, focusing on how AIP can drive automation and deliver practical solutions for everyday challenges.

Attendees were able to present their ideas to the group at the end of each day and showcase what they had built.

“This [process] takes three people a week of phone calls to compile, but this AIP Agent can now do it in minutes!” — Bootcamp attendee, reflecting on the impact of an AIP workflow on her daily tasks.

One significant outcome from the MSS Builder Bootcamps to date has been CENTCOM’s ability to apply these learnings to meet subsequent operational needs. This includes:

  • Operational AI Agent Deployment: Enabled rapid development and deployment of AI-powered agents (e.g., munitions-building advisors, network outage analyzers) directly supporting daily operational needs at the base level.
  • Empowered End Users: Analysts and operators now independently design, build, and deploy mission-critical agents after attending bootcamps — reducing reliance on external technical teams.
  • Accelerated Workflow Modernization: Teams such as NAVCENT and J6 have adopted AIP-driven solutions, modernizing workflows like ticketing and incident analysis with minimal friction.
  • Proven Path from Training to Impact: Graduates quickly transition from bootcamp (Foundry 101) to building and operationalizing AI solutions, demonstrating a clear pipeline from learning to fielded capability.
  • Increased Organizational Buy-In: High-level endorsement from previously hard-to-reach user groups following visible bootcamp-driven successes, accelerating broader adoption.
  • Sustained Innovation and Collaboration: Teams are now self-sufficient in AI solution development, leveraging internal workshops and collaborating with expert teams only when needed, fostering a culture of continuous innovation.

Palantir continues to support MSS users across CENTCOM. By delivering build-along sessions that include building pipelines from their own workflows and leveraging one-states that encompass specific concepts, Foundry data models, and AIP functions, users are equipped to address complex problem sets and streamline their operations. To date, CENTCOM users have installed over 100 MSS pre-built templates, including many templates that leverage the in-demand features provided by AIP Logic.

The Builder Bootcamps with CENTCOM illustrate the benefits of dedicated training and collaboration. By continuing to offer these bootcamps and support users in optimizing the MSS platform, Palantir is proud to support CENTCOM as it prepares a force capable of leveraging AI and data integration tools to meet future challenges.

Building with the XVIII Airborne Corps

Palantir has delivered comprehensive hands-on bootcamps to the XVIII Airborne Corps technical staff to enhance their proficiency with MSS. These trainings focus on leveraging Foundry, Ontology, and the Ontology Software Development Kit (OSDK)-based application development capabilities to address specific mission needs and operational challenges. During bootcamps, participants have built applications and data layers to enhance logistics capabilities, including informing and requesting resupply missions, and facilitating the transport of injured personnel to field hospitals with available capacity.
One significant outcome from the MSS Builder Bootcamps to date has been XVIII’s ability to apply these learnings to meet subsequent operational needs. This includes:

  • XVIII SJA Legal Workspace: Developed to streamline tracking and delegation of legal matters for the Office of the Staff Judge Advocate (SJA), this application provides centralized visibility into legal operations and investigations across the Corps. It acts as a central place for doctrine, critical data sources, and documentation of incidents, ensuring timely action and informed decision-making on critical legal issues by the SJA.
  • Medical Roles of Care Dashboard: Built to coordinate the geographic distribution of medical capabilities across units worldwide, this comprehensive tool tracks Role of Care categories with personnel counts by specialty. The workflow provides real-time personnel and equipment readiness indicators — including fill rates for providers, nurses, physician assistants, and medics, as well as critical medical equipment availability by unit — enabling commanders to rapidly assess, react, and redeploy medical personnel against current and upcoming capability gaps and support strategic planning for medical operations.
  • Surgical Consultant Portfolio: Created to track deployable medical staff across the enterprise, including their physical locations, current certifications, and medical specialties. This specialized tool enables rapid identification and mobilization of surgical expertise for deployment planning and emergency response scenarios.
  • G4 CLV Critical Munitions Forecast: Building on work initiated during XVIII’s WFX HICOM cycle and rotation at PCC-5, this application provides continued current use rates, projected shortfall visibility, and forecasting capability for critical munitions requirements. This workflow allows command to make hard decisions around prioritization and risk while ensuring supporting logistics planning and resource allocation decisions are maintained.

These applications were built within the shared MSS environment, enabling users to achieve tailored solutions across Combatant Commands and Services. Additionally, AIP-powered agents and functions can be integrated to analyze a wide spectrum of intelligence sources, helping further enhance the Corps’ analytical capabilities.

Scaling AI Capabilities for Modern Warfare Challenges

CDAO’s investment in MSS is yielding significant benefits across the Combatant Commands and Services. Palantir is proud of how quickly new users can effectively leverage MSS access to achieve customizable applications tailored to their mission needs.

Looking ahead, Palantir will continue to support and expand these training efforts, reaffirming our role as a trusted partner in advancing AI-enabled solutions that empower the Defense community.

Together, we are building a more agile, informed, and effective force, equipped to handle the complexities of modern warfare with advanced tools and expertise. Palantir’s mission to deliver, field, and scale AI capabilities is not just a promise — it is a commitment to the continued strength and effectiveness of our nation’s defense.

Empowering Combatant Commands: The Role of Maven Smart System and Palantir Builder Bootcamps was originally published in Palantir Blog on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

items.title: Ready, Set, Build with the NHS Federated Data Platform
items.hover_description:
The National Health Service (NHS) has delivered universal healthcare to an entire nation for over 75 years. With 1.5 million staff providing care to approximately 57 million patients across hundreds of hospital trusts — using decades old legacy infrastructure — the NHS is one of the most operationally complex organisations on earth.

For most of its history, the NHS has run on data that couldn’t talk to itself. Patient records, waiting lists, operating theatre schedules, discharge plans: all this critical information was stored in separate systems that NHS staff couldn’t see, couldn’t share, and couldn’t act on together, as one system. Together with the NHS, Palantir built the NHS Federated Data Platform (NHS FDP) to address this challenge.

Built to Connect Data, Safely and Securely

The NHS FDP is an NHS England programme delivered through a consortium led by Palantir. It provides a data infrastructure layer that connects the NHS to itself, bringing together operational data scattered across disconnected systems. The platform is giving clinicians, analysts, and operational staff access to the information they need, when they need it, in a secure and safe environment.

Built on Palantir Foundry, the NHS FDP operates with a federated architecture, meaning that each NHS organisation operates its own separate ‘tenant’ of the FDP, for which they are the data controller. All data therefore stays under control of the local organization while still benefiting from nationally developed digital tools and a shared ontology, called the Canonical Data Model — a single, standardised representation of the NHS ecosystem that unifies not just data, but the logic, actions, and security policies that together power how applications built atop the platform interoperate at scale. Privacy by design is at the heart of the platform: all data is encrypted, access is purpose-based, and Privacy Enhancing Technology (PET) is used to de-identify personal information whenever data flows nationally.

On the foundation provided by the platform, hospital trusts gain access to a suite of nationally developed core products — purpose-built tools for managing waiting lists, coordinating discharges, and validating patient pathways — while also gaining the ability to build their own solutions to the challenges most specific to them.

The result is a platform designed not just to process data, but to enable action, safely and securely.

Impact at Scale

The results are already visible. Hospital trusts using the platform have delivered measurable improvements across the system:

  • 110,078 additional patients have undergone procedures in hospital theatres since the FDP product has been implemented — supporting more people to receive the treatment they need to stay healthy.
  • 797,728 patients have been safely removed from NHS waiting lists using the FDP tools, helping ensure the right people are waiting for the right treatment.
  • 297,943 patients have been safely discharged from hospital using the software, with around a 15% reduction in discharge delays for patients observed since trusts started using FDP — freeing up beds for those who need them most.
  • 6.8% more patients with referrals for suspected cancer are now receiving answers within 28 days compared to the 12 months before FDP.

These numbers represent real reductions in waiting times, discharge delays, and administrative burden — and real differences in the lives of patients across England.

*Data as of end of December 2025 (updated quarterly).

Local Solutions, System-wide Impact

The core products enabled by the NHS FDP are just the beginning. What sets the platform apart is that the same infrastructure powering nationally developed tools is available to every trust to build on. The Canonical Data Model that sits at the platform’s foundation means that locally built applications can interoperate, be validated, and ultimately be scaled across the system.

A solution built by a nurse at one Trust to solve a problem on her ward can become a tool used by nurses across England. This principle — that local challenges are best solved by the people closest to them on a platform powerful enough to carry those solutions system-wide — is what the NHS FDP is built for.

From Principle to Practice

Build with FDP was created to put that vision to the test. This flagship developer event is a 48-hour hackathon bringing together engineers, analysts, clinicians, and operational staff from NHS organisations across England to explore the platform capabilities and build solutions to real problems on the NHS Federated Data Platform.

In the weeks before the inaugural event, NHS staff submitted operational challenges they wanted solved. Those problems became the foundation of the day: participants were grouped into multidisciplinary teams, each tackling a challenge nominated from the frontline, with access to the full NHS FDP toolset and support from Palantir engineers throughout.

As Ines Pinto, Product Manager at Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, put it: “The FDP, being so simple to use and intuitive, has actually created a really interesting blend between the non-technical and the technical world…you can actually integrate both in a way that’s going to make things work, because you can’t have one without the other.”

48 Hours of NHS FDP

At the inaugural event, over 120 NHS developers and analysts built 25 working prototypes on a notional version of the CDM — functional applications built from frontline expertise. A selection of the hackathon projects includes:

Early Warning System — For overstretched ward teams, the ability to act earlier — rather than react to deterioration once it has happened — is the difference between prevention and crisis. The prototype tool would help nurses identify patients at risk of clinical deterioration before it occurs. Leveraging models trained on vitals, interventions, and outcomes from across the NHS and be able to suggest proactive interventions and connect learnings system-wide.

Bed Demand Prediction — When Emergency Departments surge, reactive bed management costs time that patients don’t have. This prototype tool would enable live predictions of which ED patients are likely to require admission, enabling teams to get ahead of demand before it becomes a crisis. Trained on 300,000 rows of notional data and integrated with AI-generated recommendations based on real-time ward availability, hospitals could use the foresight to manage surge rather than just respond to it.

CAMHS Workflow Demand Balancer — In Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services, planning for demand has historically meant working from incomplete pictures and outdated data. This prototype tool demonstrated clinicians, managers, and executives could be given a live view of future demand and capacity to identify bottlenecks and surface where additional staff might be needed before problems escalate. Able to generate multiple business cases in minutes the prototype turned what was once a multi-week planning process into something operational staff could run themselves.

Genomic-Optimised Waitlist Recommendations — This prototype tool automatically flags patients on the waitlist eligible for genomic tests and determine their optimal treatment. By surfacing the right candidates at the right time, it helps ensures operational efficiency in the use of precision medicine and faster paths to effective care.

These four projects are a snapshot of what was built. Across the full 25 solutions, teams tackled everything from workforce planning and discharge risk to automated appointment booking and AI-driven clinical coding — each one a direct response to a challenge nominated by NHS staff.

Building What’s next

Each team was given the opportunity to present their project to a panel of senior NHS leaders and government representatives — including chief executives, chief information officers, and heads of data and analytics — to demonstrate what 48 hours on the NHS FDP makes possible and prove that the next chapter of digital transformation is already underway.

The NHS FDP was designed as a builder’s platform, and what the NHS developers built at the first Build with FDP event proved that they were just getting started.

The next event will take place this spring.

Ready, Set, Build with the NHS Federated Data Platform was originally published in Palantir Blog on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.
